lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Reorder the experience entries by date, with Mobility Systems Company first.
items.because: It ended in May 2025, later than the Eastern Robotics role.

items.says: Check that all dates and “Present” labels are current when the résumé is submitted.
items.because: The project begins in August 2025, after the internship ended in May 2025.

items.says: Verify that the code URL is an accessible professional profile or portfolio, not a placeholder or a link requiring extra navigation.
Make clear that “Expected” applies to the degree date, and check that the dates are current.
Clarify “around per-sensor error budgets” for readers outside the team.
Support the detection-time improvement with comparable measurement periods.
Make the claimed causal link between the dashboards and detection time defensible.
Clarify the workload or environment behind the p95 figures.
Distinguish the 200 ms build threshold from the observed 180 ms result.
The CI bullet mixes past-tense “Maintained” with present-tense “adds.”
items.because: The role has ended.

items.says: Give the release-cycle baseline and explain what “3 days” measures.
items.because: Without a comparison point, the improvement is hard to assess.

items.says: Clarify the automated checks’ role in shortening release cycles.
Separate or prioritize the migration, logging, onboarding, and on-call contributions.
items.because: The long chain of actions makes the individual contribution harder to scan.

items.says: Clarify what “removed the nightly backlogs” means.
Clarify whether the backlog result came from the migration, logging rewrite, or both.
Clarify whether “triage branch” means a software branch or a product or workflow path.
Explain what the ML-extracted features do in the system.
Give the backlog baseline and explain how the eight-week reduction was measured.
Name or define the accuracy measure if class imbalance could make plain accuracy misleading.
Explain the relevance of the domain adapter and assistant-only loss masking for the target audience.
items.because: The reader should understand the contribution.

items.says: Clarify the benchmark setup and provide the baseline latency if possible.
Explain “single-request” in the evaluation.
items.because: It may sound inconsistent with dynamic batching, which usually batches requests.

items.says: Give the GRPO latency bullet a clear subject and clarify the role.
items.because: The opening modifier does not say what or who reduced latency.

items.says: Give the latency baseline and explain how it was measured.
Explain how the training setup led to the 5% latency result.
items.because: The listed reward components do not explicitly include latency.

items.says: Provide evidence for “Stabilised” by stating what improved.
items.because: Run-to-run variance, training failures, or convergence could show the effect if measured.

items.says: Explain why one rollout per prompt was the relevant change and what result it produced.
Add an operational result or reconsider the bullet’s space.
items.because: Its impact stops at adoption, unlike the more technical, quantified bullets.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad “AI-first engineering practices” claim.
items.because: It lacks concrete evidence of what was built or how much delivery and downstream outcomes changed.

items.says: The change from 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33.3% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: A numerical mismatch can undermine confidence in the other metrics.

items.says: Clarify how latency was measured and under what workload.
items.because: Caching and answer reuse can affect latency differently with cache hits and task mix.

items.says: The rise from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not a 12% relative increase.
Include the benchmark size or evaluation conditions if available.
items.because: Readers need to judge how robust the result is.

items.says: Make the contribution and acceptance clearer than “Upstreamed.”
items.because: The term may be unfamiliar to some readers.

items.says: Clarify what the eight metrics cover and whether they were added, implemented, or both.
State which two quantities the Kendall correlation compares and in what direction.
Clarify whether the 400+ trials were unique reports or repeated perturbations.
items.because: That makes the scale and evaluation design understandable.

items.says: Identify the nature or effect of the pipeline defects more clearly.
items.because: “Structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling” is broad.

items.says: Explain the value of the fixes if there was an outcome beyond “fixed upstream.”
Add relevant tools, languages, platforms, or engineering methods actually used to the skills section.
items.because: It is short relative to the technical experience above.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific where appropriate.
items.because: It is a vague skills item.
